title: FIFO Queues
description: Implement first-in-first-out message delivery using RabbitMQ quorum queues and Amazon SQS FIFO queues.

data.text: A FIFO queue guarantees that messages are delivered and processed in the order they are sent. This sounds trivial, but most popular message brokers default to best-effort ordering. To get strong ordering guarantees you must configure the broker and the producer correctly.

Classic mirrored queues in RabbitMQ do not guarantee strict ordering across failovers. Quorum queues, introduced in RabbitMQ 3.8, use the Raft consensus algorithm. Every message is replicated to a majority of nodes before being acknowledged, which provides both durability and a single, consistent delivery order.

data.title: Node.js — Declaring a Quorum Queue
data.content: Use amqplib to declare a durable quorum queue with single active consumer.

data.text: SQS FIFO queues preserve the order of messages within a single message group. The producer sets a `MessageGroupId` — all messages with the same group ID are delivered in first-in-first-out order. Content-based deduplication is available via a five-minute deduplication window, which we will cover in the deduplication lesson.

data.title: RabbitMQ Quorum Queue vs SQS FIFO

cards.title: RabbitMQ Quorum Queue
cards.description: Ordering guaranteed by Raft consensus across replicas. Best for on-premises or self-managed deployments.
cons: Requires at least 3 nodes for production
Higher latency than classic queues due to consensus
Memory and disk overhead from replication

cards.title: Amazon SQS FIFO
cards.description: Ordering scoped to message groups. Managed service with no infrastructure to maintain.
pros: Fully managed, no servers to run
Integrated with AWS IAM and CloudWatch
cons: Throughput limited to 300 msg/s per group without batching
No push delivery — consumers must poll

data.title: Single Active Consumer
data.text: Both RabbitMQ (with x-single-active-consumer) and SQS (with one consumer) avoid the out-of-order delivery that occurs when multiple consumers race to process messages from the same group.

terms.definition: A RabbitMQ queue type that replicates messages using Raft consensus, providing strong consistency and ordering.
An SQS FIFO attribute that groups messages for ordered delivery. All messages with the same ID are delivered in order.
A queue setting ensuring only one consumer is active at a time, preventing concurrent processing that could reorder messages.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: RabbitMQ quorum queues use Raft for ordered, replicated delivery
SQS FIFO queues use MessageGroupId for per-group ordering
Single active consumer prevents concurrent reordering
Choose the broker that matches your operational and throughput requirements
data.takeaway: FIFO queues are available in both RabbitMQ and SQS, but they achieve ordering through different mechanisms and with different trade-offs.
